# tronlib

> A typed Go SDK for the TRON blockchain (Go 1.27+, gRPC to a node). One
> import for the happy path; explicit subpackages for the full surface.
> Human developers and AI coding agents are equal first-class users: every
> error carries a machine-readable code with a remediation hint, every
> example is compiled in CI and was executed on a live node, and this file
> is the curated reading order.

Module: `github.com/kslamph/tronlib/v2`

## Rules an agent must not get wrong

- Amounts are integer SUN: 1 TRX = 1_000_000 SUN. Wrap literals in
  `tronlib.TRX(n)`; parse dynamic strings with `tronlib.ParseTRX("1.5")`.
  A bare integer where a `SUN` is expected compiles — and means SUN, not
  TRX. TRC-20 amounts are separate opaque `token.Amount` values minted via
  `handle.Amount("1.6")` / `handle.Whole(3)`.
- Building, signing and broadcasting are separate steps.
  `cli.Account(owner).TransferTRX(...)` returns an UNSIGNED transaction;
  call `.Sign(signer)` then `cli.Broadcast(ctx, signed)`. The account
  handle never holds a key; owner and signer may differ (multi-sig).
- Node rejections are not Go errors: `Broadcast` returns a `Receipt` —
  check `rec.OK()` before waiting. A rejected transaction never lands, so
  `Wait` on it polls until the context deadline.
- After an ambiguous broadcast (`chain.unconfirmed`): poll `Wait(txid)`;
  do NOT rebuild and resign. Resending identical bytes is deduplicated;
  rebuilding gets a new txid and spends twice.
- TRC-20 (USDT & friends) goes through `cli.Token(ctx, addr)` with
  decimal-aware amounts. `Account(owner).TransferTRC10` is the legacy
  TRC-10 asset system, in raw asset units.
- Errors are `*tron.Error`. `Error()` prints only `op: code`, so the
  remediation is not in the message: read it with `tron.ErrorOf(err)` —
  `.Code`, `.Op`, `.Hint`, and `.Action()` (the remedy: `retry` / `wait` /
  `fix_call` / `fix_transaction` / `fund`). Match a code with
  `tron.HasCode(err, tron.CodeX)`, never by comparing message strings.

## Read in this order

- [README](README.md): the complete happy path — dial, transfer, sign,
  broadcast, wait for finality — plus the packages table and Notes that
  state the API's semantics in one line each (SUN, staking lifecycles,
  receipts, multi-sig envelopes, `With*` option rules).
- [Examples](docs/examples.md): whole-task examples — transfer, staking
  and delegation, a contract call simulated/priced/decoded end to end,
  TRC-20, permissions and offline multi-signature. Every one is compiled
  by `go test`; each is a task, not a single API call.
- [Error codes](docs/errors.md): the full code table (code → action →
  meaning) generated from source by `cmd/docgen`, plus the
  recovery-semantics legend (`retry` / `wait` / `fix_call` /
  `fix_transaction` / `fund`).
- [Architecture](docs/architecture.md): why the API is shaped this way —
  the account-scoped facade, sealed interfaces, amount safety, the
  double-spend reconciliation, and the decision log of reversed designs.

## Evidence

- [Verification ledger](docs/verification.md): every on-chain claim with
  its txid, block and the exact command to re-check it — including §3,
  what is deliberately NOT proven yet — plus the `cmd/examplecheck`
  harness that walks every documented flow against a live node.

## Maintainers

- [Runbook](docs/runbook.md): live-verification harness flags and costs,
  docgen regeneration, release gate sequence, ledger conventions.
- [Review records](docs/review.md): review dispositions and the
  consolidated deferred-work TODO list.
